us-midterms.title: U.S. Justice Department involvement intensified as the campaign reached its final stretch, deepening the divide between Democrats and Republicans
us-midterms.summary: In the United States, on the eve of the midterm elections, both parties made their final appeals to voters. Reuters and other media write that a dispute over approval in Michigan has sharpened the battle for the Senate and deepened the divide between Democrats and Republicans. Several reports say Democrats hold leading positions in a number of key Senate races, but at the same time emphasize that the outcome in the Senate remains unclear. The elections will determine control of Congress for the next two years.
us-midterms.picture: The image shows a ballot being torn by two rival hands, with scales of justice above it and a wrench caught in the machinery. It symbolizes political struggle, legal pressure and breakdowns in the election machine.

iran-hormuz.title: Iran and the United States, with Israel, are balancing on the brink of a new war over the Strait of Hormuz
iran-hormuz.summary: Iran and the United States are holding talks amid threats of a new war over the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian sources say they are ready to open the strait within two days if Washington meets the conditions, and also stress that the "ball is in the U.S. court"; contacts on ending the war continue, but without a breakthrough. Some reports say Tehran has given the government authority to dialogue with the United States. The story matters because the strait is crucial for oil and gas supplies.
iran-hormuz.picture: The image shows a giant oil tanker seemingly sliced by mines, while warships circle around it. It shows that the sea route has come close to being blocked and could become a trigger for escalation.

europe-protests.title: Youth protests continue across Europe, at times turning into riots and clashes
europe-protests.summary: In France, school protests resumed, but on a smaller scale after a two-week break. Students tried to block individual schools in Paris, Marseille and Rennes, while in recent weeks protests in France and several other European countries were accompanied by unrest and clashes. The reports also mention incidents of violence in Germany and an investigation in France after attacks with Molotov cocktails. European media describe a wave of youth discontent that in some places is spilling into street clashes.

fridge-cyberattacks.summary: Europe has again seen a series of suspected cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration equipment. According to reports, in stores in Belgium, Sweden, Luxembourg, Ireland and Estonia, temperatures in refrigerators and freezers rose sharply, in some places to very high levels. Belgium’s federal prosecutor has opened an investigation, and the European Commission has called for stronger cybersecurity. Media also note that this is not the first such incident after a similar attack in France.

ukraine-oleshky.summary: After the end of the limited ceasefire in Kherson region, the war again manifested itself both in strikes and in cyberattacks. Media report drone attacks and new casualties in several regions of Ukraine, as well as a hack of alert apps in Ukraine and Russia that spread false messages about a nuclear and chemical threat. Reuters writes that Ukraine believes Russia used the ceasefire in the Oleshky area to rearm. The reports also say no authorities have confirmed who was behind the cyberattack.

israel-election.title: Israel’s political deadlock and disputes over election legitimacy continue
israel-election.summary: Israel remains in a political deadlock after the election, and leaders are seeking a way to form a coalition. According to reports, Avigdor Lieberman backed Eisenkot for the premiership, but ruled out a minority government relying on Arab parties; the positions of Arab parties are also being discussed, as they are ready to support the opposition but are not joining the coalition. President Isaac Herzog is urging the parties to accept the results and find "creative solutions" to avoid new elections. Separate reports describe the balance of forces differently, but all agree that there is still no clear path to power.
israel-election.picture: The image shows a ballot box balancing on a tightrope, with a broken crown above it and crowds pulling ropes in different directions. It symbolizes fragile legitimacy and the struggle for power without a stable majority.

france-police-protests.title: In France and Germany, new protests and investigations follow clashes with police
france-police-protests.summary: In France, school protests were again held after the autumn break, this time on a smaller scale, but participants still tried to block educational institutions. Earlier reports speak of hundreds of arrests and an investigation under attempted murder charges after a Molotov cocktail was thrown at police. In Germany, meanwhile, acts of vandalism and clashes were also recorded amid the Europe-wide wave of protests. Overall, the publications describe a decline in intensity in France, but not the disappearance of tension.

india-protest.title: In India, the opposition is again taking to the streets against the electoral system and Modi’s government
india-protest.summary: In India, the opposition again brought supporters onto the streets, protesting against the electoral system and Narendra Modi’s government. In Delhi, mass rallies were held by Congress and an opposition alliance outraged by the removal of large numbers of names from voter rolls. AP and Reuters also report new protests against the head of the election commission. At the same time, other reports mention protests in Bangladesh and evacuations ahead of a cyclone, but the main story remains the Indian demonstrations.

binance-hack.title: After the largest cryptoasset theft, Binance is trying to hold back withdrawals and preserve client trust
binance-hack.summary: Crypto exchange Binance is trying to stabilize the situation after the largest cryptoasset theft. By various estimates, users withdrew anywhere from several to nearly five billion dollars after the hack, although the exchange later resumed operations and said withdrawals were stabilizing. TASS writes that Binance reimbursed about 95% of the stolen assets; Reuters and other media reported the scale of the theft and that it is linked to a North Korean group. The story matters because of the blow to trust in the largest exchange.

western-sahara-peacekeepers.title: The UN mission in Western Sahara ends after 35 years, and refugees await return
western-sahara-peacekeepers.summary: The UN mission in Western Sahara has ended after 35 years because the Security Council did not renew its mandate. AP and Reuters report that the mission’s end followed a diplomatic dispute in the Security Council, while the territory itself remains contested between Morocco and the Polisario Front. For refugees in camps in southern Algeria, this means fresh uncertainty and hope of return that they have waited for for decades. The story is important as the end of one of the UN’s longest peacekeeping presences.
western-sahara-peacekeepers.picture: The image shows an empty UN helmet lying next to an almost packed refugee suitcase, with closed gates ahead and a distant house key. It is an image of the mission’s end and an unfulfilled return home.

hong-kong-markets-ai.summary: China and Hong Kong are stepping up measures to support markets and are betting on AI and financial technologies. Bloomberg writes that Chinese authorities are expanding tools to support the stock market and trying to strengthen its stability and confidence. Separate reports from Hong Kong say night trading in derivatives is expanding, fintech strategy is developing and there is interest in AI, as well as contacts between Meta and the local regulator over smart glasses. Against this backdrop, U.S. pressure and trade risks continue, as stated directly in parts of the reports.

gaza.title: Israeli strikes on Gaza are again killing civilians
gaza.summary: Civilians in Gaza have again been killed as a result of Israeli strikes. Reuters reports four dead, while the BBC says eight were killed, including a child; sources also give different numbers and locations of the strikes, including Khan Younis and Gaza. The reports agree that the attacks continue and that among the victims are not only fighters but also civilians. This is important as another confirmation of the heavy cost of the ongoing conflict.

south-africa-elections.title: In South Africa, key local elections became a test for the governing ANC and coalitions
south-africa-elections.summary: South Africa has begun key local elections that are seen as a test for the governing ANC and its ability to govern through coalitions. Reuters writes about vote fragmentation and the battle for cities, while AP calls the vote a serious test for the ruling party. Technical problems were also reported: in some places polling stations opened late, ballot boxes were stolen and there were ballot delivery errors. The elections matter for the distribution of power in the cities and for the reputation of the electoral system.

south-korea-ai-defense.summary: South Korea is increasing its focus on AI, defense and drones amid the North Korean threat and broader economic uncertainty. Yonhap reports the creation of a new government drone team, talks with Japan and the United States on security issues, and efforts to strengthen industrial competitiveness. uganda-somalia-withdrawal.summary: Uganda has begun withdrawing its troops from Somalia after 20 years of participating in the African Union mission. BBC says Uganda was the first to send soldiers to the mission, created to help stabilize Somalia in 2007; Reuters has confirmed that the pullout has already started. It marks a significant stage in a long international security operation in the region.

According to AP, Reuters, BBC and other outlets, the 20-year-old Mercedes driver secured the title after the race in Mexico, where he finished third. Media describe it as a historic achievement and note that this is only his second season campaign. The victory matters above all as a new motorsport record.

world-trek-man-returns-home.title: Briton completes 28-year round-the-world walk and returns home
world-trek-man-returns-home.summary: Briton Karl Bushby has completed a 28-year walk around the world and returned home to Hull. Reuters, BBC and The Guardian write that he crossed dozens of countries and thousands of miles, beginning his route in 1998. The reports stress that the journey included extremely difficult stretches and many challenges, and that he has now become the first person to walk continuously around the planet. It is an unusual story of endurance and the completion of a years-long journey.

Euronews writes that skeletons, zombies and film characters marched through Greenwich Village, turning the procession into a vivid city spectacle. It is above all a festive event that draws large crowds of spectators and participants.

greenland-airport-opens.summary: A new international airport has opened in Greenland and is expected to attract tourists. AP writes that the project is also tied to the island’s long-term plans for the future and possible independence. The story matters as an infrastructure step that could change the region’s accessibility.

bhutan-stupas-volunteers.summary: In Bhutan, thousands of volunteers built 108 stupas in Gelephu Mindfulness City in a single day.
